segments.title: Georgia Smart Set, Bunk Johnson and White's own featured solos
segments.summary: White recalls Bunk Johnson on the Georgia Smart Set and describes his own New Orleans-style features and triple-tongue solos.

segments.title: Lizzie Miles and the circus at the State Fair
segments.summary: White describes Lizzie's act with white pigeons and his work as Miles's bandmaster splitting the band between the big show and the side show.

segments.title: Arrested without his draft card in Missouri and sent to Camp Funston
segments.summary: White tells of being jailed for lacking his registration card and being sent on to camp.

segments.chapter: Army service and the 816th Pioneer Infantry Band
segments.title: Arrival at Camp Funston, the sergeant's slap and the typing test
segments.summary: White describes the slap at the gate, reporting to the major, and being picked out for office work and then for musicians.

segments.chapter: Army service and the 816th Pioneer Infantry Band
segments.title: Winning the bandmaster's job of the 816th Pioneer Infantry Band
segments.summary: In an elimination contest White impressed the lieutenant and was made bandmaster; the band toured by train on Liberty drives to Camp Upton.

segments.chapter: Army service and the 816th Pioneer Infantry Band
segments.title: The band's players, Maurice Durand and the voyage to France
segments.summary: White names his trumpet and other players, Durand's Livery Stable Blues feature, and the trip across England and France.

segments.chapter: Army service and the 816th Pioneer Infantry Band
segments.title: Verdun, Harry Truman, Pershing and the return from Le Havre
segments.summary: White tells of concerts at Verdun, serenading Truman, the Montfaucon cemetery with General Pershing, his status as bandmaster, and the wait in Le Havre.

segments.title: Heading to New Orleans and marrying Hazel Robinson
segments.summary: After discharge White went to New Orleans, where he married Hazel Robinson in 1920.

segments.title: Working as a printer in New Orleans and meeting Buddy Petit and Arnold Metoyer
segments.summary: White talks his way into a job at Garnier's print shop, prices the work, prints for musicians, and meets Buddy Petit and Arnold Metoyer.

segments.chapter: Corrections and views on early Black music
segments.title: Library of music and corrections to a published story about White
segments.summary: After a tape break the talk turns to his music library and errors in an earlier article, such as being a night watchman or jailed.

segments.chapter: Corrections and views on early Black music
segments.title: Honorable service record and later invitations to rejoin Army bands
segments.summary: White cites his citation letter and offers to have joined regular Army bands, including one at Fort Huachuca.

segments.chapter: Corrections and views on early Black music
segments.title: Comparing James Reese Europe's band with Will Vodery's 807th and jazz in France
segments.summary: White rates Europe's band for entertainment and Vodery's for military music, and discusses who introduced jazz to the French.

segments.chapter: Corrections and views on early Black music
segments.title: Sidney Bechet, William Marion Cook, Mary Wayne and Eugene Michael
segments.summary: The two discuss Bechet's trip with Cook, then White praises Cook, Mary Wayne's orchestra and his teacher Eugene Michael over Europe.

segments.chapter: Corrections and views on early Black music
segments.title: Disputing Duke Ellington's claim about Black reading musicians
segments.summary: White disputes that there were no reading Black pianists before 1915, citing Tony Jackson, Michael, Murray and Smalls's father in Charleston.

segments.chapter: Corrections and views on early Black music
segments.title: Wendell McNeil and John Robichaux's orchestras in New Orleans
segments.summary: White recalls playing trumpet for Wendell McNeil's society band, the engagements and dress code, and John Robichaux's playing.

segments.chapter: Corrections and views on early Black music
segments.title: Dr. Locke's book and the record of early Black bands
segments.summary: White says Locke should retract his statements and that his own travels give him knowledge of the bands.

segments.title: Blind Boone, Charleston music teachers and church music
segments.summary: White names Blind Boone and the Charleston teachers who trained him, and describes the city's churches, organs and choirs.

segments.title: Scott Joplin at Atlantic City and Alonzo Hardy
segments.summary: White says he knew Joplin, who brought four rags to the Jenkins band at Atlantic City and gave them to bandmaster Alonzo Hardy.

segments.title: Closing: what the Jenkins orphanage made possible
segments.summary: White credits the orphanage training for his career and the interview ends with thanks.
